The REFUTED status is justified as a material-support judgment at the supplied stage. The respondent's own statement supports that he asserted a bona fide residential requirement, but the allowed record contains express prior-court findings accepting the contrary plea and stating that both Tribunals treated the claim as not bona fide. The row correctly preserves those as prior-court findings and expressly avoids treating them as target-High-Court approval. The later findings on insufficiency and suitability of the landlord's existing accommodation do not, under the supplied law, supply an operational bona fide standard that would negate the recorded prior-court refutation.

The SUPPORTED status is justified for the literal occupation-route test. DRC_BONA_FIDE-C03 is disjunctive, and the supplied record expressly describes the respondent's proposed occupation as his own residential occupation. That is sufficient material support for the landlord-self route without inferring dependency of the identified family members. The status does not establish bona fides under C02 or the full clause-(e) claim.

The UNSUPPORTED status correctly records absence of affirmative material for the separate beneficiary-person route. No allowed source identifies a person for whose benefit the premises are held. The row also correctly avoids converting the absence of this alternative route into either affirmative refutation or a failure of legal support for the landlord-self route, which is separately addressed under C03 and C04. Unsupported is retained separately, not relabeled negative or unresolved.
